doc.title: Spiegle Willcox and Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Norwich, New York, November 14, 1995

title: Pay in the twenties and thirties compared
summary: Gallodoro got $235 a week from Whiteman in 1936; Willcox compares his pay with Whiteman's Collegians, the Ramblers and Goldkette; they discuss hotel costs on the road.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Isn’t that interesting. You see the difference in the ages right there.
Now you’re talking about 1936, and you made how much?

Now here we go. Back in 1923, with the Paul Whiteman Collegians, in 1923, six nights a week, I made a hundred bucks a week. And now wait. And with the California Ramblers a hundred and a quarter, and then with the Goldkette a hundred the first year, and then when I came back I— But see now the Goldkette band was in 1925 so the first year I made a hundred, Bill Rank, he made a hundred, and you know. And then from 1925 ‘til 1936, inflation was going. That’s how you got to $235.
Did you have to cover your own expenses when you were on the road?

No, no. Oh, hotel you had to pay yourself. But the hotel rooms then were about three dollars, single, and we used to get a rate for two and a half. Some good hotels, not flea bags. Decent hotels. Like the Gibson in Cincinnati.
